theme_name: Rules On The Operation Of The Vehicles
chapter_name: Admission To Road Traffic Vehicle Documents Driving Licence
question_text: What documents do you have to carry with you, if you want to drive a compulsory registrable vehicle?

options.text: The registration certificate Part I (Motor Vehicle Registration)
The registration certificate Part II (Motor Vehicle Title)

correct_answers.text: The registration certificate Part I (Motor Vehicle Registration)

comment: As a car driver, you must always have your driver's license and vehicle registration certificate (certificate of registration part 1) with you. The vehicle title (registration certificate part 2) should be kept safely at home. It serves as proof of ownership and is not needed while driving.

theme_name: Rules On The Operation Of The Vehicles
chapter_name: Admission To Road Traffic Vehicle Documents Driving Licence
question_text: A technical modification to your vehicle means that the operating licence is extinguished. What consequences should you anticipate if you nevertheless use the vehicle on public roads?

options.text: An entry into the Central Register of Road Traffic Offenders
The loss of my insurance cover

correct_answers.text: An entry into the Central Register of Road Traffic Offenders
The loss of my insurance cover

comment: If you use your vehicle on public roads despite the expired operating license, you will lose your insurance cover because the vehicle is no longer the one that was originally insured. Since there is an obligation to have insurance in Germany, driving without insurance is a misdemeanor. In the event of a police check, a fine will be imposed and you must expect an entry in the register of fitness to drive.

theme_name: Rules On The Operation Of The Vehicles
chapter_name: Admission To Road Traffic Vehicle Documents Driving Licence
question_text: An inspection has been performed because of a technical modification made to your vehicle. What are you obliged to do?

options.text: - carry the inspection report or confirmation in my vehicle, and have the registration in certificate Part I corrected if necessary
- forward the inspection report or confirmation to the vehicle manufacturer
- stick the inspection report or confirmation into the designated place in the registration certificate Part II

correct_answers.text: - carry the inspection report or confirmation in my vehicle, and have the registration in certificate Part I corrected if necessary

comment: After the technical modification of a vehicle, an acceptance report is usually created during the assessment. However, an entry may also be made in part 1 of the certificate of registration. The protocol must be carried by the vehicle driver during each journey. On request, the protocol must be presented, for example, during a stop-and-search operation.

theme_name: Rules On The Operation Of The Vehicles
chapter_name: Admission To Road Traffic Vehicle Documents Driving Licence
question_text: An assessment is required following modifications to your vehicle. When must this be performed?

options.text: At the time of the next inspection
When demanded by the registration authority

comment: The assessment must be carried out immediately after the conversion.

theme_name: Rules On The Operation Of The Vehicles
chapter_name: Admission To Road Traffic Vehicle Documents Driving Licence
question_text: The suspension of your motor vehicle has been lowered and an expert opinion must be obtained. When is this required?

options.text: Together with the next official inspection (Hauptuntersuchung), at least 1 year after the alteration
When requested by the vehicle licensing authority

comment: If you lower a car you need this change on the chassis to be officially accepted. Therefore, the assessment must be done immediately. You must always carry the report or confirmation with you and, if necessary, have this technical change registered in the certificate of registration part 1, the registration certificate.

theme_name: Rules On The Operation Of The Vehicles
chapter_name: Admission To Road Traffic Vehicle Documents Driving Licence
question_text: You are holding a driving permit class B. Your car has the following specifications: - empty mass 1900 kg - permissible total mass 2400 kg - permissible towed load 1500 kg Which trailer are you allowed to tow?
comment: Regardless of the information, a vehicle plus a trailer may only have a restricted total weight of 3,500 kg for a Class B driving license. When the car is fully loaded, the loaded trailer must not weigh more than 1,100 kg. Exception: The car has a maximum permissible mass of 3,500 kg and the trailer weighs less than 750 kg.
